status: Each definition appears once. Runtime reuse additionally requires identical relevant bindings and contexts.

views.title: Proposed · Tricks, lead and score

nodes.label: Best next move
nodes.summary: Compare legal moves by the average difference between our final game score and theirs.
nodes.returns: Selected move, conditional plan and qualified comparison
nodes.detail: This is a proposed playing-phase model. Candidate coverage and unfinished comparisons are reported separately. Bidding and exchanges should later call the same consequence model from their own legal successor contexts.
nodes.epistemic: A choice supported by estimated candidate values and their bounds. Selecting it deterministically proves neither that it will win nor that it is truly optimal.

nodes.label: Expected score advantage
nodes.summary: Average our final game score minus the opponents’ score across the represented continuations. Higher is better.
nodes.returns: Expected game-score difference, outcome probabilities and unresolved bounds
nodes.detail: Game score includes the contract reward or penalty and the defenders’ scored points. It is different from raw card points. For example: our -160 minus their 215 = -375. Against 250 it is -410; the first result is 35 better. Model probabilities and incomplete coverage remain explicit. Branch weights are applied exactly once to conditional terminal scores. Unfinished branches retain explicit bounds and mass; they are not dropped and the remaining mass is not silently renormalised.
nodes.epistemic: An estimate under the joint hand, response and continuation models. Exact arithmetic does not prove the future score or the real-world accuracy of this expectation.

nodes.label: Who takes the later tricks?
nodes.summary: Continue from each joint trick outcome, comparing what the next leader can do and what each seat can reasonably choose afterwards.
nodes.returns: Unweighted conditional terminal outcomes, or unfinished branches with bounds and trace identities
nodes.detail: A trick winner, captured points, consumed cards and information stay on the same branch. Future tricks are conditioned on earlier outcomes. Their separate marginal probabilities must not be multiplied.

bindings.continuation: Reapply the same trick model at the successor context after the selected next action.
bindings.progress: Each repeated trick consumes cards; legal declaration steps have explicit rights and no zero-progress question loops.
bindings.terminal: Accumulate actual card points, credited pair points, last trick and contract outcome before final scoring.
bindings.weighting: Preserve conditional branch identities and response likelihood factors. Only value integrates these into the final expectation; do not average twice.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Who wins the next trick?
nodes.summary: Resolve each legal response sequence and retain the winning seat together with the points, spent cards and observations.
nodes.returns: Joint trick-outcome branches, not four independent winner chances
nodes.detail: Two branches won by the same seat may leave very different hands and opportunities. Keep them distinct unless their relevant successor behaviour is equivalent. The engine determines the exact winner inside each legal branch.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Which moves are legal now?
nodes.summary: Read the acting seat’s legal cards, questions and announcements from the engine.
nodes.returns: Candidate action set with actor and phase
nodes.detail: The first graph covers play and declaration decisions. It does not claim a complete auction or exchange model. A declaration before a card changes the context for the trick query.
nodes.epistemic: Known only from the permitted observations and exact deductions in the bound context. Hypothetical context facts remain conditional.

nodes.label: Which cards will the seats play?
nodes.summary: Process seats in actual order. Apply forced replies directly and predict genuine choices from the acting seat’s information.
nodes.returns: Ordered legal response branches and conditional likelihoods
nodes.detail: A player’s visible context is updated after each card, not only after the complete trick. Later opponents may overruff earlier players. A partner’s ability to win does not imply they choose the necessary card.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Who must follow or overtake?
nodes.summary: Combine exact playing rules with possible hands to establish mandatory following, overtaking or trumping in each branch.
nodes.returns: Forced legal replies with proven and uncertain parts distinguished
nodes.detail: An opponent who must follow cannot instead ruff. A partner’s earlier void is no longer present if a passed-back card refilled that suit.
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: Choices between legal replies
nodes.summary: Compare the acting seat’s possible legal responses under a named finite response model.
nodes.returns: Legal response distribution or declared approximation
nodes.detail: Responses obey the actor’s own view. A finite base level prevents recursive best-response calls from expanding without bound. No access to the actual partner’s backend store or private intent.

bindings.perspective: The can_beat and forced queries bind to this responding actor and its filtered posterior after the preceding cards. A different root-only belief may not supply its choice inputs. Equal actor information, intent and model imply equal response distributions.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Who can beat the winning card?
nodes.summary: Check higher following cards, available trumps, overruffs and remaining actors in the trick.
nodes.returns: Joint winning and interrupting conditions
nodes.detail: The same joint allocation supports following and trump ownership. Do not multiply separate suit and ace probabilities. Exposed-state capability queries are not automatically behavioural response probabilities.
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: Who leads after this trick?
nodes.summary: The actual winning seat obtains the next lead opportunity in that branch.
nodes.returns: Seat-specific next leader
nodes.detail: Our team winning is not enough when only one partner can use the required announcement or side entry. Obtaining lead does not restore spent declaration rights.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Which points does each team take?
nodes.summary: Credit the trick’s cards and, where applicable, the last-trick bonus to the winning team.
nodes.returns: Captured points attached to the same outcome branch
nodes.detail: These points feed final game scoring. They are not added as a separate heuristic bonus to final score advantage.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Which cards and rights remain?
nodes.summary: Apply the actual cards spent, pair halves broken, depleted suits and rights consumed along the branch.
nodes.returns: Successor resources, separately projected to each actor
nodes.detail: Winning with a trump Ace and winning with a low trump are different resource outcomes even if the same player leads next.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: What does each seat learn?
nodes.summary: Filter public actions and private evidence for each actor after every transition.
nodes.returns: Actor-permitted observation histories
nodes.detail: An exposed void can become a hard fact. Private hands and another live agent’s reasoning stay hidden. The exact unknown allocation is not an observation.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Beliefs after those observations
nodes.summary: Condition joint beliefs on newly observed plays and hard deductions, with remaining hand capacities.
nodes.returns: Successor hard support and joint posterior measure
nodes.detail: A discard may alter several suits’ probabilities. A complete soft estimate of one is still different from universal proof over hard-consistent states.
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: What can the next leader do?
nodes.summary: Evaluate the leader’s legal opportunities with the actual remaining cards and rights, under the updated information.
nodes.returns: Available continuation bindings for that successor
nodes.detail: A retained pair can be inaccessible; a previously weak suit may now provide a standing run. Newly available alternatives must be discovered even when the old plan is still legal.
nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Compare the next sequences
nodes.summary: Compare cashing winners, changing or passing the lead, delaying or making declarations, and disrupting an opponent’s route.
nodes.returns: Conditional policies with explicit resources and interruption branches
nodes.detail: These are parameterised action families, not mandatory tactics or point bonuses. Omitted legal continuations remain a coverage limitation.
nodes.epistemic: Candidate selection under qualified estimates; no certainty about success or universal optimality is implied.

nodes.label: Which remaining cards are standing?
nodes.summary: Check remaining higher ranks and relevant ruff threats under the successor trump and suit distribution.
nodes.returns: Proven winners or joint conditions for becoming winners
nodes.detail: The context includes trump. A same-suit top card can still face a ruff. A proposed trump switch requires a fresh query, while unchanged hard facts can be reused.
nodes.epistemic: Proven only when no hard-consistent legal counterplay can beat the specified run. Otherwise its success is a model estimate; zero soft mass is not proof.

nodes.label: Cash or develop a winning run
nodes.summary: Compare collecting current winners with drawing out blockers so another card becomes a winner, while accounting for who keeps the lead.
nodes.returns: Bounded candidate sequences and outcome dependencies
nodes.detail: Cash-first is not always best. The chosen cards can spend entries or expose a pair; each sequence is evaluated through the same joint trick model.

bindings.program: Bind legal lead -> joint trick query at this successor -> observe leader/resources -> compare next cash/development step or stop.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Draw trump before a side lead
nodes.summary: Compare removing opposing trump threats against the winners and entries spent to do it.
nodes.returns: Finite draw prefixes and stopping alternatives
nodes.detail: The prefix is unavailable without established trump. It stops on changed opportunity, resource loss or a better compared continuation. It is not an always-draw rule.

bindings.program: Bind current-trump lead -> joint trick query -> condition on observed result -> compare continue versus side lead or another action.
bindings.progress: Each completed iteration consumes cards and a trick.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Let the required partner lead
nodes.summary: Compare following-suit entries and ruff entries, including the opponents’ legal interventions and the pair/entry cards that must survive.
nodes.returns: Seat-specific lead-transfer policies and failures
nodes.detail: The query asks who actually wins. Partner holding trump is not enough. A passed-back card can force partner to follow, and a later void opponent can overruff.

bindings.program: Bind proposed lead -> joint trick query -> test desired winning seat with consumed resources -> compare the following cash/declaration/return-entry opportunity.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: When can a pair actually score?
nodes.summary: Compare legal own announcements, questions and delays, with the right actor on lead and both halves still available.
nodes.returns: Credited pair events and changed-trump successor contexts
nodes.detail: Pair possession is not scored possession. After an announcement, evaluate tricks and entries under the new trump. Opponents can also obtain an opportunity to announce.

bindings.program: Bind holder/questioner and uncalled suit -> legal actor choice/response -> apply announcement or answer -> joint trick model under changed trump; compare delay using current-trump continuation.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: Interrupt an opponent’s route
nodes.summary: Compare taking the lead, drawing a critical winner, forcing expenditure of a pair half, or letting an opponent retain an unhelpful lead.
nodes.returns: Counterplay candidates scored by complete consequences
nodes.detail: No automatic bonus for capturing a trick or denying a pair. A cheap lost trick can be preferable if it preserves a stronger continuation.

bindings.program: Bind an identified opponent entry/winner/declaration dependency -> enumerate legal plays affecting it -> joint trick and continuation query -> compare final scores.

nodes.epistemic: A hypothetical consequence or continuation. Exact engine transitions hold within a branch; which branch occurs remains uncertain.

nodes.label: One choice for the same information
nodes.summary: Future decisions cannot depend on a hidden difference the acting player has not observed.
nodes.returns: Permitted grouping of decision contexts
nodes.detail: Distinct hidden allocations may require one shared action. Do not optimise separately with knowledge of each complete deal and then average those oracle results.
nodes.epistemic: A constraint on permissible reasoning. It does not assert which hidden world or future observation will occur.

nodes.label: How likely is each joint branch?
nodes.summary: Carry initial joint allocation mass through conditional response and observation branches.
nodes.returns: Branch weights and unresolved mass
nodes.detail: A branch includes winner, captured points, resources and information together. Alternative action success probabilities do not have to sum to one; outcome weights within one complete candidate model do.

bindings.measure: Initial joint hand mass times successive conditional response likelihoods for the same candidate and observable trajectory. Observation partitioning preserves mass. Sum mutually exclusive paths; do not multiply independent winner marginals.
bindings.identity: Candidate, full bound trajectory/observation context, observer and response/model versions. A branch weight for one action is not a weight for another.

nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: Score in each possible outcome
nodes.summary: Apply contract success or failure, defenders’ scoring, rounding and Schwarz to the complete game outcome.
nodes.returns: Our game score minus the opponents’ game score

inputs.label: card points on that same trajectory

nodes.detail: Credited pairs and final contract outcomes also come from each completed continuation. Never treat a current partial point total as a terminal result. This first objective is the current game; series payouts use a separate horizon.

bindings.inputs: Accumulated card and pair points, actual final contract and declaring side, trick counts and existing rule settings, from the same terminal branch.

nodes.epistemic: Exact conditional calculation for a fully specified terminal outcome. It is not knowledge that this outcome will occur. A partial trajectory yields a separate estimate or bound.

nodes.label: Joint possible hands
nodes.summary: Weight only allocations consistent with the actor’s exact knowledge, retaining correlations between cards and suits.
nodes.returns: Hard support plus a named joint belief measure
nodes.detail: Zero model weight does not remove a hard-consistent possibility from proof. Query or transition equivalence is required before grouping allocations.
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: What the acting seat knows
nodes.summary: Project the hypothetical seat’s own hand and permitted history, with its model of other players.
nodes.returns: Scoped knowledge, beliefs and response inputs
nodes.detail: This is root’s hypothetical model of another seat. It does not share the real partner’s backend knowledge or plan.
nodes.epistemic: Own permitted observations and demonstrably shared facts can be known. Unknown parts of another seat’s information and its beliefs are modelled hypotheses, separately labelled.

nodes.label: Observed cards and certain deductions
nodes.summary: Own hand, personally seen transfers, public play and exact deductions constrain all reasoning.
nodes.returns: Actor-local information and proven constraints
nodes.detail: Real observations, hypothetical assumptions and future successors keep distinct scopes. An identical fact query can be reused across branches whose relevant inputs have not changed.
nodes.epistemic: Certain relative to the observer and stated evidence. An assumed branch fact stays conditional; it never enters the actual knowledge base as an observation.

nodes.label: Trump, acting order and rights
nodes.summary: Read the led suit/current trick, trump, next actor and surviving question/announcement rights in the bound context.
nodes.returns: Deterministic rule context
nodes.detail: This definition can be called in different successor states. Same label does not imply the same runtime query or cache entry.
nodes.epistemic: Known only from the permitted observations and exact deductions in the bound context. Hypothetical context facts remain conditional.

nodes.label: Bid and exchange interpretations
nodes.summary: Use observed conventions as fallible joint evidence within the hard constraints.
nodes.returns: Likelihood factors and model identity
nodes.detail: Knowledge of a passed card is exact. Deduced intent from choosing that pass is uncertain and must be modelled separately.
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: Known scoring rules
nodes.summary: The engine defines card values, pair credits, contract scoring, rounding and Schwarz.
nodes.returns: Deterministic scoring function and active rules
nodes.epistemic: The rule is known. Applying it to an assumed future produces a conditional score, not a known future result.

views.status: Authored definitions for review; not an execution trace

views.title: Current · Does partner hold a pair?

nodes.label: Does partner hold this pair?
nodes.summary: The current ConceptQuery API can answer a holding question with separate proof and model probability fields.
nodes.returns: Hard truth, conditional truth, probability bounds and resolution
nodes.detail: This does not calculate whether partner gets the lead, chooses to ask, activates a pair and wins the contract. Those strategic dependencies are currently composed in procedural policy helpers.
nodes.epistemic: Separate fields: hard truth over all permitted allocations; truth conditional on a premise; probability under the soft model. A probability of 1 alone is not a hard proof.

nodes.label: Every permitted allocation
nodes.summary: Exact deductions define which hidden holdings remain possible from this seat’s information.
nodes.returns: Hard support; proof includes zero-soft-weight cases
nodes.epistemic: Known only from the permitted observations and exact deductions in the bound context. Hypothetical context facts remain conditional.

nodes.label: Joint weighted allocations
nodes.summary: Belief queries integrate joint allocation weights rather than treating pair halves as independent cards.
nodes.returns: Conditional weighted mass with unresolved bounds
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: Pair, with optional conditions
nodes.summary: Pair means both King and Ober held by the named seat; conditions may also constrain cards, voids and counts.
nodes.returns: Canonical signed holding predicates and conditions
nodes.detail: Conjunctions and conditions share card-count constraints. This schema does not yet author action sequences or compare their scores.
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.

nodes.label: What this seat has observed
nodes.summary: Own hand, public play and transfers visible to this actor feed exact deduction.
nodes.returns: Private seat view and exact constraints
nodes.epistemic: Known only from the permitted observations and exact deductions in the bound context. Hypothetical context facts remain conditional.

nodes.label: Observed bid and exchange signals
nodes.summary: Existing convention models assign weights within hard-consistent support.
nodes.returns: Joint belief model parameters and factors
nodes.epistemic: Estimated under the stated joint belief model. Any proof is reported separately over all hard-consistent possibilities.
